_note: Operator declarations for instance two. Each declaration turns an Unresolved fact into a conscious Assumed, never a Confirmed (CLAUDE.md §12.2). Written by the 'Anonymised consortium with fictional gap partners' ticket in plans/dev_graph_demo_tickets.md; later tickets append the duration, the effort shares and anything else they leave open. The engine reads this file and never writes it. Schema: .claude/workflows/system_orchestration/artifact_schema_specification.yaml -> tier3_source_schemas.working_assumptions.

Its capabilities trace to the instance-one Part B-1, held outside the repository, but nobody has confirmed its participation in instance two. Derived partner. University, geoinformatics institute; country slot C1 (Member State). Capability evidenced by the instance-one Part B-1, participation unconfirmed.
Derived partner. University, agriculture; country slot C1 (Member State). Capability evidenced by the instance-one Part B-1, participation unconfirmed.
Derived partner. SME, software engineering; country slot C1 (Member State). Capability evidenced by the instance-one Part B-1, participation unconfirmed.
Derived partner. SME, farm-management information systems; country slot C1 (Member State). Capability evidenced by the instance-one Part B-1, participation unconfirmed.

Derived partner, and the second country slot. Public research institute, vegetable crops; country slot C2 (Member State). It held no in-action role in instance one, so its role here is designed rather than carried over.

Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. Public research organisation, freshwater ecology; country slot C3 (Member State). Closes the freshwater gap: the derived six have no freshwater expertise, and the scope asks for capabilities across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems.

Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. University, marine and coastal science; country slot C4 (Associated Country). Closes the marine gap and supplies the only route to a marine occurrence data facility.

Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. University, biodiversity genomics; country slot C5 (Member State). Closes the omics gap: the second expected outcome names genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic data, and the derived six carry only metabolomics.

Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. Non-profit research organisation, biodiversity data infrastructure; country slot C3 (Member State). Closes the data-infrastructure gap: nothing in the derived six can carry the cooperation with the named in-situ data frameworks, the typology crosswalks or the open-science-cloud link.
Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. University institute, socio-ecological systems; country slot C6 (Associated Country). Closes the socio-ecological gap the third scope requirement opens.

Fictional gap partner. It does not exist. SME, earth observation analytics and artificial intelligence; country slot C5 (Member State). Closes the European-scale artificial-intelligence mapping and trend-prediction gap the first and third expected outcomes both open.

P01 holds the science spine of the derived capability set. The artifact schema requires exactly one coordinator and Phase 6 needs one to attach a management structure to. Declared so it can move without contradicting a Confirmed fact.

declarations.rationale: Six pseudonymous country slots, four Member State and two Associated Country. A slot records nothing but its class, which is all the Tier 1 composition condition asks about. The mapping from slots to real countries is held outside the repository, and for the six fictional partners there is nothing to map.

The Tier 1 condition needs three independent beneficiaries in three countries, one in a Member State. The derived six span two slots and fail it. Every partner that adds a third country is fictional and Assumed, so the condition is met only on the strength of these declarations. Evaluated by runner/consortium_composition.py and reported in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/validation_reports/demo-consortium-gap-analysis_2026-09-30.json.

_value_note: A declaration's 'value' carries the fact the operator declares, not its status. The status is Assumed for every declaration and the shared reader stamps it (runner/working_assumptions.py DECLARED_STATUS), so writing 'Assumed' into 'value' would both duplicate it and break the schema's contract: the W1 predicate compares 'value' against a claim's claim_summary. Each *_participation value is derived from the partner's own record in partners.json, so a declaration cannot drift from the registry.
